questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Urban Local Bodies' refers to.
questions.a: Cities and towns are run by urban local bodies, elected municipal councils and corporations that provide services like water, roads, waste removal and street lights for millions of residents.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Urban Local Bodies'.
questions.a: A city's needs are too many for any one office: elected local bodies divide the work ward by ward.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Urban Local Bodies' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Municipal Corporations and Municipal Councils' refers to.
questions.a: Big cities are governed by municipal corporations, smaller towns by municipal councils and nagar panchayats; each is elected, raises local taxes and keeps records for its area.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Municipal Corporations and Municipal Councils'.
questions.a: The size of the settlement decides the shape of its body: corporations for metropolises, councils for towns.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Municipal Corporations and Municipal Councils' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Wards and Councillors in a City

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Wards and Councillors in a City' refers to.
questions.a: Each city is divided into wards, and every ward elects a councillor; councillors together form the municipal body, decide budgets and bye-laws, and answer to the ward's residents.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Wards and Councillors in a City'.
questions.a: Wards shrink a huge city to a human scale: every locality gets one voice in the civic body.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Wards and Councillors in a City' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Participatory Democracy in Cities' refers to.
questions.a: Urban governance aims at participatory democracy: citizens, not just officials, take part in city functioning through elections, ward meetings and feedback, so that administration stays answerable to residents.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Participatory Democracy in Cities'.
questions.a: Good city governance empowers citizens to participate, not merely to receive services.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Participatory Democracy in Cities' taught, and from which source text?
